label: copy-phase re-input of "e" in short sequences (weak, unexplained)
explanation: Very sparse feature (0.03% of steps). About 2/3 of activation mass is in the copy phase, and about 62% of it falls on steps where the fed-back input is "e". It is enriched at recall_idx 1, i.e. when "e" was the first original token, and in short sequences (L 3-5). The strongest examples are e.g. "e s i b <DEL> [e] s", with the output token often s/n/z. There is also a smaller, scattered original-phase component on varied tokens (n, j, a, b, d...) near the end of the original input. Never fires at t<3 and almost never on the delimiter. Precision is poor (~4%): most copy-phase "e" inputs in short sequences do not activate it, and adding conditions on the output or next token did not separate active from inactive cases. Best dev F1 is ~0.1, so the input-e description is a weak correlate, not an explanation. Magnitude varies little (median 0.12, max 0.25); the top activations are the e-at-recall_idx-1 cases.
